name: Auditory-Motor Developmental Plasticity
short_description: Auditory-motor connectivity supporting beat perception is shaped by a sensitive period before age 7 — early musical training produces lasting structural changes that later training cannot achieve
higher_order_principle: The auditory-motor system that underlies beat perception (ASAP, M10) has a sensitive period in childhood. This is analogous to the critical period for language acquisition: the brain's capacity to forge auditory-motor connections has enhanced plasticity during early childhood. Early rhythm exposure during this window produces permanent advantages; equivalent training begun later produces functional but not structural changes.

neural_substrate.corpus_callosum: Interhemispheric auditory-motor coordination — enhanced myelination with early training

developmental_trajectory.infancy_0_12mo: Preference for rhythmic regularity; meter discrimination present; behavioral entrainment imprecise
developmental_trajectory.toddlerhood_1_3yr: Spontaneous movement to music appears but synchronization is poor
developmental_trajectory.childhood_4_7yr: Beat synchronization ability emerges; sensitive period for structural changes
developmental_trajectory.late_childhood_8_15yr: Complex meter processing, syncopation perception, groove sensitivity develop

sensitive_period.early_training_effect: Permanent connectivity enhancement in corpus callosum and corticospinal tract
sensitive_period.late_training_effect: Functional improvement but less structural change

causal_links.evidence_base: Bailey, Zatorre, & Penhune (2014, ~200 citations): Early training linked to gray matter structure in ventral premotor cortex. Structural changes do not occur with equivalent training begun after age 7.
Penhune (2011, ~400 citations): Sensitive period evidence. Longitudinal studies show lasting effects of early training.

scope_conditions: Applies to musical training effects on rhythm processing
Sensitive period boundaries are approximate (~7 years), not absolute cutoff
Genetic variation contributes substantial variance independent of training
moderators: Type of musical training (rhythm-focused vs. melodic)
Intensity and duration of training during sensitive period

interactions.nature: M11 describes how the auditory-motor connectivity underlying M10 ASAP develops
